title: Pretoria to Boca Chica: the Emigrant, the Factories, and the Light of Consciousness
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Pretoria, the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested. The pin is the canonical Pretoria pin, -25.7461, 28.1881, inherited byte-identical from joshua_haldeman.journey.json; it differs by about four kilometres from the city coordinate carried by the geography pass, and the corpus pin is used so the two files sit on one point.
stops.campa: Elon Reeve Musk is born in Pretoria, the administrative capital, first child of Errol Musk, an engineer, and Maye Haldeman, a model and dietitian married the year before. On his mother's side the family has been in the Transvaal twenty-one years. Her father, Joshua Haldeman, flew his own aircraft from Canada to South Africa in 1950 and opened a chiropractic practice in this city, in a country he had chosen for its politics. The grandfather is sixty-eight, and the boy will keep no direct memory of him. He dies in a light aircraft near Pretoria in January 1974.
suggested_refs: The canonical Pretoria pin, -25.7461, 28.1881, shared across the corpus

stops.name: Waterkloof House Preparatory School, the reader
stops.date_confidence: the school is attested; biographers give the span only as approximately 1977 to 1983, and the month and day are defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: He goes to school in the Waterkloof suburb and reads the way other children eat. Biographers record him working through the household encyclopaedia and then whole shelves of science fiction, holding pages nearly verbatim and correcting adults out loud when they are wrong. He is disliked for it at school, and he does not stop doing it. His parents divorce in 1979, when he is eight, and the household after that splits between Pretoria, Johannesburg, and a stretch in Durban that the biographies place at city level and no closer. He chooses to live with his father.
suggested_refs: Waterkloof House Preparatory School, Pretoria

stops.name: Bryanston High School, the stairwell
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Biographers place him at this Johannesburg school in the mid-1980s without exact years, and Vance and Isaacson do not agree on whether the assault happened here or at Pretoria Boys High. The disagreement is carried, not resolved. Month and day defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: He is at a Johannesburg school through the worst of his adolescence. A group of boys corner him at the top of a stairwell, beat him, and throw him down it; the injuries are serious enough that both his biographers treat the episode as a hinge in the life. He spends these years being hunted at school, in a country where schoolyard violence of that order surprised nobody. Which campus it happened on, Vance and Isaacson do not agree, and neither does the family. The record leaves it open.
suggested_refs: Bryanston High School, Johannesburg; and Pretoria Boys High School, the two campuses the sources disagree between

stops.name: Pretoria Boys High School, the exit planned
stops.date_confidence: the school and the 1986-1988 span are attested; month and day defaulted to 1 January. The coordinates are corrected to the school's own address, 251 Roper Street, Brooklyn, Pretoria, from the approximate pin carried by the geography pass, which fell about a kilometre away.
stops.campa: He finishes secondary school on Roper Street, isolated, teaching himself to program on a machine bought with saved money. Around him the apartheid state is conscripting white boys his age into the South African Defence Force: finish school, and the army has him for two years, to be used against the majority of the people in the country. His mother was born in Canada, which makes him eligible for a Canadian passport by descent. He starts the paperwork before he has finished the exams.
suggested_refs: Pretoria Boys High School, 251 Roper Street, Brooklyn, Pretoria

stops.name: Pretoria, the passport and the departure
stops.date_confidence: his arrival in Canada is attested to June 1989; the date of his departure from South Africa is not separately recorded and is placed in the same month. The pin is the canonical Pretoria pin.
stops.campa: In June 1989, seventeen years old, he goes. The route out runs through his mother's Canadian citizenship, claimed by descent and processed slowly enough that he waits months on a single document while the call-up gets closer. He leaves with very little money, no place arranged at the far end, and no intention of returning to a country that would hand him a rifle for a purpose he refuses. Maye follows in time, and Kimbal, and his sister Tosca. Errol Musk stays in South Africa, and the argument between father and son goes on from separate continents for the next thirty-five years.
suggested_refs: The Canadian citizenship-by-descent claim of 1989, the mechanism of the emigration

segments.name: Kingston, Philadelphia, and Two Days at Stanford

stops.name: Queen's University, Kingston
stops.date_confidence: the year of entry is attested; month and day defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: He enrolls at Queen's in eastern Ontario and works his way through a run of Canadian jobs, some of them filthy, in the year and a half before the term starts and during it. He discovers he can talk to strangers if the subject is large enough. The plan is already the United States, on the reasoning that whatever he means to do is done there, and he stays two years. Here he meets Justine Wilson, a fellow student who intends to be a novelist and does become one, and who writes afterward about how hard he pursued her.
suggested_refs: Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario

stops.name: University of Pennsylvania, the two degrees
stops.date_confidence: the 1992 transfer and the 1997 conferral of both degrees are attested, the latter by the PayPal registration statement he signs in 2002; month and day defaulted to 1 January. The two-year gap between his leaving Philadelphia and the degrees being awarded is recorded by the sources and explained by none of them.
stops.campa: He transfers to Penn in 1992 and reads for two degrees at once, physics in the college and economics at Wharton. He is in Philadelphia three years, sharing a house with Adeo Ressi that the two of them run as a paying party venue on weekends to cover the rent, and then he leaves for California in 1995. Neither degree is conferred until 1997, once outstanding requirements are settled; the registration statement he signs for PayPal in 2002 gives that year for both. Two years stand between the leaving and the awarding, and no source reached here accounts for them.
suggested_refs: PayPal Inc., Form S-1 registration statement, 2002, giving the 1997 conferral dates

stops.name: Stanford, the enrollment that may not have happened
stops.date_confidence: contradiction carried, not resolved, and the stop is tagged [R]. Wikipedia, fetched 2026-08-24, states he was accepted to a graduate program in materials science at Stanford in 1995 but did not enroll. Musk's own account, repeated by Vance and Isaacson, is that he enrolled and left after about two days. No registration record has been produced by anyone. The month is a placement on the start of the academic year.
stops.campa: He is accepted to a graduate program in materials science and applied physics, meaning to work on high energy-density capacitors for electric cars. He arrives in the Bay Area the year Netscape goes public. In the version he has told for thirty years he registers and quits within two days, unable to sit still while the internet is being built a few miles up the peninsula. Stanford's records show no enrollment at all, and Wikipedia states flatly that he never enrolled. Whether he ever sat in a classroom on this campus is not settled by anything either side has produced.
suggested_refs: Stanford University graduate admissions, materials science, 1995: acceptance attested, enrollment unrecorded

stops.name: Zip2, Palo Alto
stops.date_confidence: the founding year is attested; the month is a placement inside 1995
stops.campa: With his brother Kimbal and Greg Kouri he founds Global Link Information Network, renamed Zip2: searchable city guides licensed to newspapers that have not yet understood what is about to happen to their classified advertising. They rent one small office. Musk sleeps in it, writes the first version of the software himself, and for a long stretch will not let the hired engineers touch his code without his going over it afterward. Four years later Compaq buys the company.
suggested_refs: The Zip2 office on Sherman Avenue, Palo Alto

stops.name: Palo Alto, twenty-two million dollars
stops.date_confidence: the month and the figures are attested; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: The Compaq acquisition closes in February for about 307 million dollars in cash, bought for the search technology Compaq wants under its own portal. Musk's stake, roughly seven percent, returns about 22 million dollars to a twenty-seven-year-old who arrived in North America ten years earlier with nothing worth listing. He does not stop working and he does not diversify. Within months about 12 million dollars of it is committed to the next company. That is most of what he has.
suggested_refs: Compaq Computer Corporation's acquisition of Zip2, February 1999

stops.name: X.com, Palo Alto
stops.date_confidence: the founding year is attested and the geography pass places the incorporation in March 1999; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: He incorporates X.com to do to retail banking what Zip2 did to the classifieds: one account holding everything, run over the web, with the branch network deleted. He keeps the letter, and twenty-four years later he will paint it on a social network. In March 2000 X.com merges with Confinity, a company on the same street whose money-transfer product is called PayPal and whose engineers prefer Unix to his Windows stack. He loses the argument about the operating system, and the argument about which product the merged company actually is.
suggested_refs: The X.com and Confinity offices on University Avenue, Palo Alto

stops.name: Palo Alto, removed while away
stops.date_confidence: the month and year are attested; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: He has married Justine Wilson earlier in the year, a writer he met as a student in Kingston. While the two of them are away on their honeymoon the board of the merged company removes him as chief executive and puts Peter Thiel in the seat, over the product question and the operating system and the way he runs a room. He hears about it in transit. The company renames itself PayPal in 2001, dropping his letter from the door. He does not sue, does not sell, stays the largest shareholder, and keeps coming into the building.
suggested_refs: The September 2000 board action replacing Musk with Peter Thiel

stops.name: PayPal headquarters, North First Street, San Jose
stops.date_confidence: the acquisition year is attested and October is the closing month given by the geography pass; the day is not recorded. The coordinate is PayPal's own headquarters at 2211 North First Street, substituted for the generic San Jose civic-centre coordinate carried by the source pool.
stops.campa: eBay buys PayPal for 1.5 billion dollars in stock. Musk, the largest single shareholder, clears somewhere between 175 and 180 million dollars before tax, and the money arrives at a company whose name is no longer his and whose direction has not been his for two years. By now he has been removed from the top job at two companies he started. He is thirty-one. In the same year he is naturalized as a citizen of the United States and registers a company to build rockets.
suggested_refs: PayPal Inc., Form S-1, 2002; the eBay acquisition of October 2002

stops.name: Moscow, the rockets that were not for sale
stops.date_confidence: the trips are attested to 2001 and 2002; the sources give no single agreed date for either, and November 2001 is a placement inside the attested span
stops.campa: He flies to Moscow with Jim Cantrell and Adeo Ressi to buy decommissioned intercontinental ballistic missiles, meaning to land a small greenhouse on Mars and broadcast the picture of the first green thing grown on another planet. The Russians take the meetings. They also quote him a price that rises each time he asks, and he leaves without a rocket. On the flight home he starts costing the raw materials of a launch vehicle himself, and finds that the metal, the fuel, and the electronics come to a small fraction of what launches are sold for.
suggested_refs: The 2001-2002 Moscow negotiations for surplus Dnepr launch vehicles

stops.name: Hawthorne, Space Exploration Technologies
stops.date_confidence: the founding year is attested; May is the month generally given and the day is not recorded in the sources used here
stops.campa: He puts roughly a hundred million dollars of the PayPal money into a rocket company and hires Tom Mueller, who has been building liquid engines in a garage, then Gwynne Shotwell and Hans Koenigsmann. The premise is vertical integration: engines, airframes, avionics, and software made in one building, so that none of the margins stacked up by fifty years of cost-plus contracting are paid to anybody. The building is a former Boeing fuselage plant beside the freeway in Hawthorne, and the desks sit out on the open factory floor, within sight of the hardware.
suggested_refs: The former Boeing 747 fuselage plant at 1 Rocket Road, Hawthorne, California

stops.name: Los Angeles, ten weeks
stops.date_confidence: tagged [R]. The death is very widely reported and was not re-verified against a primary source in the research pass. Neither the exact date nor the place is established in any source reachable here, and the Los Angeles city coordinate is a placement rather than a record; September 2002 orders the stop and carries no evidential weight.
stops.campa: Nevada Alexander Musk, his and Justine's first child, dies of sudden infant death syndrome at ten weeks old. Musk does not speak about it in public for years, and when he does he says he dealt with it by refusing to deal with it. Justine writes about it at length afterward, and about what the refusal was like to live beside. Five more children follow within four years, twins and then triplets, all conceived by in vitro fertilization. Neither the date nor the place of the death is established in any source reached here, and this pin is a placement rather than a record.
suggested_refs: Justine Musk, 'I Was a Starter Wife' (Marie Claire, 2010)
sources: researched dossier, flagged as independently unconfirmed in the verification pass

stops.name: Omelek Island, three failures
stops.date_confidence: the first Falcon 1 launch attempt is attested to 24 March 2006; the second and third failures, of March 2007 and August 2008, are carried inside this stop's campa rather than given stops of their own
stops.campa: SpaceX launches from a coral islet in Kwajalein Atoll, two thousand miles from Hawaii, because the American ranges will not give a new company a slot. Engineers live in tents, ship parts across the Pacific in containers, and dive for cooling. Falcon 1 fails on its first flight when a fuel line leaks and the engine burns through seconds after liftoff. It fails again in March 2007 on stage separation. In August 2008 the stages collide in flight and the third rocket is lost with them. The money is nearly gone.
suggested_refs: Omelek Island launch site, Kwajalein Atoll, Marshall Islands

stops.name: Omelek Island, the fourth flight
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On 28 September 2008 Falcon 1 reaches orbit on its fourth attempt. It is the last flight the company can pay for. Tesla is days from insolvency the same autumn, the credit markets have frozen, and Musk has divided what is left of his own fortune between the two companies rather than let either die, borrowing from friends to make payroll. Weeks after the launch NASA awards SpaceX a Commercial Resupply Services contract to carry cargo to the International Space Station.
suggested_refs: Falcon 1 Flight 4, 28 September 2008; the NASA CRS award that followed

segments.name: The Pads, and the Case for Mars

stops.name: Cape Canaveral, the first stage comes back
stops.date_confidence: the date is attested. The source pool gave the place only as 'Cape Canaveral, Florida'; the coordinate supplied here is Landing Zone 1, the concrete pad the booster actually touched down on.
stops.campa: Nine minutes after lifting eleven Orbcomm satellites, the first stage of a Falcon 9 turns around in the upper atmosphere, flies back down through its own exhaust plume, and sets itself upright on a concrete circle at Cape Canaveral. The industry has spent sixty years dropping its hardware into the sea. Within a few years reflight is ordinary, single boosters fly ten and then twenty times, and the floor price of a kilogram to orbit moves for the first time since Apollo. In the Hawthorne control room, on the night itself, the shouting drowns out the launch commentary.
suggested_refs: Landing Zone 1, Cape Canaveral: Falcon 9 flight 20, Orbcomm OG2 M2, 21 December 2015

stops.name: Expo Guadalajara, making humans multiplanetary
stops.date_confidence: the address is attested to 27 September 2016 and its publication in New Space to June 2017; the geography pass tagged the venue [R]
stops.campa: At the International Astronautical Congress he presents the Interplanetary Transport System: a reusable booster and ship sized to put a hundred people at a time on Mars, aiming at a self-sustaining city of a million people. Nothing in the slides exists yet, though nine years on a version of it is flying and exploding over Texas. The talk is printed the following year, with the figures, in the journal New Space. Under oath years later, asked what SpaceX is for, he gives the same answer he gives from this stage, in almost the same words.
stops.quote: [t]o extend the light of consciousness beyond Earth in a sustained, permanent manner
stops.quote_source: Musk deposition at 117:10-16, describing the mission of SpaceX, quoted in Tornetta v. Musk, C.A. No. 2018-0408-KSJM (Del. Ch.), slip op. at 15 n.55
suggested_refs: Elon Musk, 'Making Humans a Multi-Planetary Species,' New Space 5, no. 2 (June 2017), 46-61
sources: Tornetta v. Musk, Del. Ch. post-trial opinion, courts.delaware.gov id=359340

stops.name: Launch Complex 39A, the car in solar orbit
stops.date_confidence: the source pool gives only the year 2018; 6 February 2018 is the launch date of the Falcon Heavy demonstration flight and is supplied here to place the stop
stops.campa: Falcon Heavy flies for the first time from the pad that launched Apollo 11, twenty-seven engines lighting together, and the two side boosters come back and land side by side within a second of each other. A demonstration flight carries no customer, so the mass simulator can be anything at all. This one is Musk's own cherry-red Tesla Roadster, thrown onto a heliocentric orbit that crosses the orbit of Mars and tracked from Earth ever since, with a mannequin in a pressure suit sitting at the wheel.
suggested_refs: Falcon Heavy demonstration flight, 6 February 2018, Kennedy Space Center LC-39A

stops.name: Boca Chica, the steel yard on the border
stops.date_confidence: SpaceX selected the Boca Chica site in 2014 and Starship development flights begin from it in 2019; month and day defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: At the mouth of the Rio Grande, on a flat of tidal mud and dune between a wildlife refuge and the Mexican border, SpaceX builds spacecraft out of stainless steel in the open air. Starship is meant to be entirely reusable, to lift a hundred tonnes, and to be the machine that makes the Mars arithmetic close. The early prototypes explode on the pad, on landing, and in flight, and the explosions are televised. Musk calls each one the cheapest available way to buy information. The company keeps building the next hull while the last one is still smoking on the flat.
suggested_refs: The Starship production and launch site at Boca Chica, Cameron County, Texas

stops.name: Launch Complex 39A, two astronauts
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken ride a Crew Dragon to orbit from 39A: the first people launched from American soil since the shuttle stopped flying in 2011, and the first ever launched on a spacecraft built and operated by a company rather than a state. For nine years the only route to the station had been a Russian seat, bought by NASA from the same agency that would not sell Musk a missile in 2002. Eighteen years earlier the industry's settled view of him was that he was a rich amateur who would lose his money and go away. NASA now buys seats from him by the flight.
suggested_refs: NASA Commercial Crew Program, Demo-2, 30 May 2020
sources: NASA Commercial Crew Program press materials

stops.name: Starbase, the town incorporates
stops.date_confidence: attested: the incorporation vote of 3 May 2025 and the formal incorporation of 20 May 2025 are both recorded
stops.campa: The settlement around the launch site becomes a city of Cameron County, Texas, by a vote of its residents, most of whom work for SpaceX. A SpaceX vice-president, Bobby Peden, is elected mayor unopposed; the two commissioners run unopposed as well, and also work for the company. Musk had announced the intention four years earlier and none of it is concealed at any point: it is a company town, chartered in the open, on the last dry ground before the Gulf. The vote is held on 3 May 2025 and the city is incorporated on the twentieth.
suggested_refs: Starbase, Texas: incorporation election of 3 May 2025, incorporation 20 May 2025

segments.name: The Car, the Battery, the Sun

stops.name: San Carlos, the Series A
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 2004; the day is not recorded. The figure varies between about 6.35 and 6.5 million dollars across sources and both are carried.
stops.campa: Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning incorporated the company the year before and named it for Nikola Tesla, whose alternating-current induction motor is what their car will actually run on. Musk leads the first financing round with roughly six and a half million dollars, takes the chairmanship, and takes the seat that lets him decide what the product is. In 2014 he will give a million dollars and a charging station to the museum being made of Tesla's ruined Wardenclyffe laboratory on Long Island, the tower the man went bankrupt building and never finished.
suggested_refs: Tesla Motors Series A, February 2004; the 2014 gift to the Tesla Science Center at Wardenclyffe, Shoreham, New York

stops.name: San Mateo, SolarCity
stops.date_confidence: the founding year is attested; the month is a placement. The geography pass tags this [R] because Musk's part is the founding concept, the capital, and the chairmanship rather than daily presence in the building.
stops.campa: His cousins Lyndon and Peter Rive found a residential solar installer on his suggestion and with his money. He chairs the board and does not run it. The logic is a closed loop: panels on the roof, a battery in the garage, a car in the driveway, all of it sold by companies he controls. In 2016 Tesla buys SolarCity for about 2.6 billion dollars. Shareholders sue, calling it a bailout of a failing company owned by the buyer's own family, and after trial the Delaware court finds for him.
stops.quote: expedite the move from a mine-and-burn hydrocarbon economy towards a solar electric economy
stops.quote_source: Elon Musk, 'The Secret Tesla Motors Master Plan (just between you and me)' (Tesla blog, 2006), his stated overarching purpose, quoted in Tornetta v. Musk (Del. Ch.), slip op. at 12 and n.17, citing JX-48 at 1
suggested_refs: In re Tesla Motors, Inc. Stockholder Litigation (Del. Ch. 2022), the SolarCity acquisition trial
sources: Delaware Chancery opinion, In re Tesla Motors/SolarCity (2022)

stops.name: Fremont, the plant nobody wanted
stops.date_confidence: Musk became chief executive in October 2008 and the initial public offering is attested to June 2010; the Fremont purchase and reopening fall in late 2010 and the day is not recorded
stops.campa: Tesla buys the shuttered NUMMI plant, five and a half million square feet that General Motors and Toyota ran jointly and then walked away from, for a small fraction of what building it would cost. Musk has taken the chief executive's job in October 2008 and taken the company public in June 2010, the first American carmaker to float since Ford in 1956. Seven years later the Model 3 line in this building falls so far behind that he puts a fourth assembly line in a tent on the parking lot, moves a bed onto the factory floor, and sleeps there for months.
stops.quote: As of 2016, the number of American car companies that haven't gone bankrupt is a grand total of two: Ford and Tesla.
stops.quote_source: Elon Musk, 'Master Plan, Part Deux' (Tesla, 2016), quoted verbatim in Tornetta v. Musk, C.A. No. 2018-0408-KSJM (Del. Ch.), courts.delaware.gov id=359340
suggested_refs: The former NUMMI plant, 45500 Fremont Boulevard, Fremont, California

stops.name: Gigafactory Nevada, Storey County
stops.date_confidence: the grand opening of 29 July 2016 is attested; construction ran from 2014 and limited Powerwall production began in January 2016. The longitude is corrected from the -119.453 carried by the geography pass, which fell about a kilometre west of the site.
stops.campa: In the desert east of Reno, on a site with no town attached to it, Tesla and Panasonic build a battery plant sized by arithmetic rather than by demand: to sell electric cars in the millions, somebody has to make more lithium-ion cells per year than the entire world currently makes. Construction starts in 2014, the first Powerwall packs come off the line in January 2016, and the plant is opened formally that July. The building is designed to have the largest footprint on Earth and is never completed to the drawing. It is the first factory Musk builds rather than buys.
suggested_refs: Giga Nevada, Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County

stops.name: Lingang, the Shanghai plant
stops.date_confidence: groundbreaking 7 January 2019 is attested, with initial production in October 2019 and first customer deliveries on 7 January 2020. The longitude is corrected from the 121.937 carried by the geography pass, which fell some sixteen kilometres east of the site, out toward open water.
stops.campa: Ground is broken at Lingang on 7 January 2019 and cars are coming off the line before the year is out, on land granted and credit arranged by a state that has decided electric vehicles are a national industry and that this foreigner may own his factory outright rather than through a joint venture. No other carmaker is given those terms. Within a few years Shanghai is Tesla's export hub and its highest-volume plant. The company's largest single manufacturing dependency is now a government.
suggested_refs: Gigafactory Shanghai, D203A Tonghui Road No. 168, Nanhui New Town, Lingang, Pudong

stops.name: Austin, the headquarters moved
stops.date_confidence: construction began July 2020, limited production August 2021, the headquarters move was announced at the annual shareholder meeting in October 2021, and the delivery event called Cyber Rodeo was 7 April 2022. The source pool placed the headquarters move in 2020, which is the year of Musk's own relocation to Texas and not the company's; the correction is carried here.
stops.campa: He announces at the annual meeting that Tesla is moving its headquarters from Palo Alto to a half-finished factory on the Colorado River east of Austin. The Texas plant opens with a party called Cyber Rodeo in April 2022. With Fremont, Nevada, Shanghai, Berlin, and Austin he has a manufacturing base no new carmaker has assembled in a century. He had moved himself the year before, selling nearly every house he owned and keeping one, in Hillsborough, which he cannot rent out.
stops.quote: I tried to put it on Airbnb, but they banned Airbnb in Hillsborough. They're so uptight.
stops.quote_source: Musk deposition at 118:14-21, explaining under oath why he owns only one house, quoted in Tornetta v. Musk (Del. Ch.), courts.delaware.gov id=359340
suggested_refs: Gigafactory Texas, 13101 Tesla Road, unincorporated Travis County
sources: Tornetta v. Musk, Del. Ch. opinion, courts.delaware.gov id=359340

stops.name: Grunheide, the plant in the pine forest
stops.date_confidence: the plant opened in March 2022; the source pool gives only the year, and 22 March is the recorded opening date
stops.campa: Tesla clears pine plantation in Brandenburg for its first European plant and meets a country with a different theory of speed: water-authority objections, a drinking-water association in court, protest camps in the trees, and permits issued provisionally and then issued again. The factory is built anyway, in about two years, on the edge of a protected groundwater zone. Local opposition over how much water it draws does not end when the plant opens.
suggested_refs: Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg, Grunheide, Mark

segments.name: The Tunnel, the Implant, the Machine Mind

stops.name: Pioneer Building, San Francisco: OpenAI
stops.date_confidence: the founding announcement is dated 11 December 2015. The coordinate is corrected to the Pioneer Building's own address, 2185-2199 Folsom Street, from the pin carried by the geography pass, which fell about 430 metres north-east.
stops.campa: In a red brick building in the Mission, Musk, Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Ilya Sutskever set up a nonprofit laboratory whose stated purpose is to see that if artificial general intelligence arrives it does not arrive owned by one company. Musk pledges money and gives as his reason that unaligned machine intelligence is an existential risk to the species. When the laboratory converts to a capped-profit structure and takes Microsoft's money he sues it, and later builds a competitor of his own. He had left its board in 2018.
suggested_refs: The Pioneer Building, 2185-2199 Folsom Street, San Francisco; OpenAI vacated it in August 2024

stops.name: Pioneer Building, San Francisco: Neuralink
stops.date_confidence: Neuralink was founded 21 June 2016 and was headquartered in this same building until 2022, when it moved to Fremont. The source pool carried a single 'Fremont/San Francisco' pin that conflated the two eras; the founding is placed here at the Pioneer Building and the Fremont period is named in the campa.
stops.campa: Six months later, in the same building, he founds Neuralink with eight others to put electrode threads into human brains. The purpose follows from the last one: if machine intelligence cannot be prevented, then widen the channel between it and the person, so that people are participants rather than pets. The company moves to Fremont in 2022. In May 2023 the Food and Drug Administration authorizes a first human trial, and on 29 January 2024 Noland Arbaugh, paralyzed from the shoulders down, is implanted and learns to move a cursor by thinking about it.
suggested_refs: Neuralink at the Pioneer Building, 2016-2022; the first human implant, 29 January 2024

stops.name: Hawthorne, the hole in the parking lot
stops.date_confidence: The Boring Company was founded 11 January 2017 as a SpaceX subsidiary and spun off in 2018; the Hawthorne test tunnel was dug between 2016 and 2018
stops.campa: Stuck in Los Angeles traffic, he posts that he is going to build a tunnel boring machine and start digging, and then does, in the lot beside the SpaceX factory. The test tunnel runs 1.14 miles. The company pays for early work partly by selling novelty flamethrowers, and later digs the Vegas Loop under the Las Vegas Convention Center, where Teslas with human drivers carry conventiongoers between halls at low speed. Most of the announced projects, in Chicago, Los Angeles, San Jose, and Miami, are quietly abandoned.
stops.quote: Mr. Musk estimates he split the bulk (at least 90%) of his work hours, approximately 80 to 90 hours per week, between Tesla and SpaceX, with an allocation of 60% to Tesla and 40% to SpaceX. He allocated his remaining work hours (8-9 hours per week) between Neuralink, The Boring Company and Open AI.
stops.quote_source: Musk's Amended Responses and Objections to Plaintiff's First Set of Interrogatories, 3 August 2020, JX-1256 at 34, quoted in Tornetta v. Musk (Del. Ch.), courts.delaware.gov id=359340
suggested_refs: The Boring Company test tunnel, Hawthorne, California, 2016-2018

stops.name: South Memphis, Colossus
stops.date_confidence: xAI was founded in July 2023; Colossus was built at the former Electrolux plant on Paul R. Lowry Road in South Memphis during 2024, the cluster assembled in 122 days and brought online between July and September 2024. The source pool's coordinate fell about fifteen kilometres away in central Memphis and its date of 2023 preceded the site; both are corrected.
stops.campa: He founds xAI in July 2023, and a year later fills a dead Electrolux plant in South Memphis with roughly a hundred thousand graphics processors in a hundred and twenty-two days, which is not a schedule the data-centre industry recognizes as possible. The cluster trains Grok. stops.campa: On 7 August 2018 he posts that he is considering taking Tesla private at 420 dollars a share, and that funding is secured.
